correctness.rationale: An idempotent P gives a direct sum of image and kernel. The weight −1 identity on each same-summand pair is precisely closure of that summand, and on mixed pairs both sides vanish. Since J³=0, an element a1+j with a≠0 has a polynomial relation with nonzero constant term expressing 1 as a linear combination of its positive powers. Exactly one summand of a complementary subalgebra pair therefore contains the unit. In J, the determinant product is alternating also in characteristic two; all lines are subalgebras and a plane is closed exactly when it contains Kz, since otherwise its projection to J/Kz is onto. The possible ordered dimensions and unit placement now give exactly the four isolated pairs and four incidence families. The GL₂ change on J/Kz moves any ordered transverse pair of directions to any other; a central shear matches the lift of the line without changing the plane containing Kz. This proves transitivity in each family, and ranks together with unit placement and the distinguished subspaces K1,J separate the eight orbits. The planes number q+1 and each admits q² transverse lines. Over any field the fibers are the affine planes of complements to T in J, locally trivial by choosing a fixed transverse vector on a chart. An independent F₂ replay enumerated 24 subalgebras, checked all 52 ordered complementary projections against idempotence and the 16 basis-pair identities, and found ranks (1,13,24,13,1) and orbit sizes (1,1,1,1,12,12,12,12). broader_coverage.reasoning: Splitting specifies how such operators arise, not the complementary subalgebras or their conjugacy classes. For the indexed symmetric-form family, the exterior product on J/Kz is alternating and nonzero, hence symmetric in characteristic two, but skew and not symmetric in odd characteristic. Thus the broader symmetric-form theorem covers a genuine parameter subcase, not the entire exterior-algebra result.

The supported distinct contribution is the arbitrary-field conjugacy classification of the idempotent weight −1 locus with its incidence-orbit sizes and uniform field count. The distinct indexed symmetric-form result independently covers the characteristic-two labeled incidence classification and rank polynomial as a special case, but does not give the all-field exterior-algebra orbit classification. value.rationale: Once splitting is known, the natural classification question is which complementary pairs are equivalent under algebra automorphisms. This gives all eight orbits, not just a matrix list or a point count for one field, and explains their sizes over finite fields via the same incidence geometry in every characteristic. The extension to characteristic two respects its change in commutativity; the prior overlap of labeled counts in that one regime does not exhaust the classification.
